question: An article is marked at ₹950. If it is sold at a discount of 20%,then the selling price becomes 2.5 times of its cost price. What is the cost price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) = 80% of Marked Price (MP)

SP = 0.8 × 950 = ₹760

Given, SP = 2.5 × Cost Price (CP)

⇒ 760 = 2.5 × CP

⇒ CP = 760 ÷ 2.5 = ₹304

**∴ The correct answer is ₹304.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹950

Discount = 20%

Selling Price (SP) = 2.5 × Cost Price (CP)

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = ?
 
 
 MP = 950
 
 
 SP = 760

 

 -20%

 

 SP = 2.5 × CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 950 × (100 − 20) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 950 × 80 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 950 × 0.8

⇒ SP = ₹760

⇒ 2.5 × CP = 760

⇒ CP = 760 ÷ 2.5

⇒ CP = 7600 ÷ 25

⇒ CP = ₹304

**∴ The correct answer is ₹304.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is an allowance given on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. The selling price after discount is given as SP = MP − Discount.

Profit & Loss Base Rule

Profit or Loss percentages are universally computed using the Cost Price (CP) as the base value unless a different condition is explicitly mentioned. Formula: SP = CP + Profit.

Mark-up Formula

Mark-up indicates how much the price has been raised above the cost price to determine the marked price. Mark-up amount = MP − CP.
